newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle close mixed, feeders mostly up.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle close mixed, feeders mostly up.

text.p: CME live cattle futures ended mixed with nearbys buoyed by cold weather while feeder cattle closed mostly higher on thin short covering, traders said.
Live cattle closed 0.100 cent a lb higher to 0.250 lower with February ending up 0.100 at 63.975 cents. Feeder cattle finished 0.025 lower to 0.175 higher with only January off at 66.500 cents.
Renewed weather concerns and strength in wholesale beef prices at noon provided light support in live cattle futures late, traders said.

Live cattle had slipped early as the market appeared overbought on weather concerns late last week, especially with heavy snowfall staying much further to the north than expected. But the forecast for bitter cold weather to dip well into Texas prompted renewed concern that weather would curb weight gains and further limit the already-tight supply of choice-grading cattle.
The weather, plus a modest rebound in beef prices at midday after a long period of declines, underpinned futures.
Lighter-weight choice beef was quoted at $104.63 per cwt, up $0.33 at noon after posting its lowest level since September 5 late Friday.

Traders also noted that activity in futures was starting to wind down ahead of USDA's Cattle-on-Feed report Friday and the upcoming holiday period. Early analysts' estimates on the report for major feedlots of 1,000 head or more point to on-feed numbers on December 1 at 102 to 104 percent of a year ago, November placements between 98 and 109 percent and November marketings between 91 and 98 percent of a year ago.

Cargill Investor Services bought February and Prudential Securities sold. In live cattle options, there were active risk reversals, buying of April 62 and 64 puts and selling of 66 and 68 calls, pit sources said.
Feeder cattle continued to be influenced by action in live cattle and firmed again late on scattered short covering in thin dealings, traders said.
Refco bought January light and R.J. O'Brien bought March. FIMAT Futures USA sold May. Cargill Investor Services spread long June live cattle/short March feeders, pit sources said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was up $0.15 at $65.02 per cwt.
